paper_title: High-density polyethylene—an inert additive with stabilizing effects on organic field-effect transistors

knowledge_points.content: Binary blends of semicrystalline high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and organic semiconductors like DPP-TT-T or N2200 can be used to fabricate high-performance p-type and n-type transistors with improved mechanical and environmental stability.
knowledge_points.evidence: Here, we demonstrate that binary blends comprising the semicrystalline high-density polyethylene (HDPE) in combination with hole- and electron-transporting organic semiconductors allow fabrication of p-type and n-type thin-film transistors of notably improved device stability and, in some scenarios, improved device performance.

knowledge_points.content: A 1:1 blend of N2200 and HDPE achieves an electron mobility in the saturation regime (μsat) exceeding 2 cm²/V·s, which is more than double the mobility of neat N2200 (0.9 cm²/V·s).
knowledge_points.evidence: The electron mobility in the saturation regime (μsat) in blends exceeds 2 cm2 V−1 s−1 in our best device, while OTFTs fabricated with neat N2200 exhibit a μsat = 0.9 cm2 V−1 s−1.

knowledge_points.content: The addition of HDPE to DPP-TT-T significantly improves the subthreshold slope (Ss-th) from approximately 600 mV/dec in neat films to 200 mV/dec in blends containing 95 wt% HDPE.
knowledge_points.evidence: the subthreshold slope, Ss-th, to become notably steeper, from ≈600 mV dec−1 for the neat semiconductor, to ≈200 mV dec−1 for blend layers comprising 95 wt% HDPE.

knowledge_points.content: Blending DPP-TT-T with 50 wt% or more HDPE reduces the interfacial trap density (NT) from 2.1 × 10¹² eV⁻¹ cm⁻² (for neat polymer) to as low as 0.3 × 10¹² eV⁻¹ cm⁻².
knowledge_points.evidence: NT shows a dramatic reduction in blend devices as summarized in Table 1. [Table 1 shows 0 wt% = 2.1 and 50 wt% = 0.3 in units of 10^12 eV-1 cm-2]

knowledge_points.content: The crystallization sequence is critical for blend performance; the semiconductor must be forced to crystallize while the HDPE is still in the liquid phase (solution or melt) to ensure unhindered formation of charge transport pathways.
knowledge_points.evidence: The deposition temperature has to be chosen such that the semiconductor is forced to crystallize while the insulator is still in the liquid phase, solution or melt... This is followed by crystallization of the insulator which assists producing percolation pathways.

knowledge_points.content: In situ grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) reveals that in P3HT:HDPE blends cast at 100 °C from decalin, P3HT crystallizes within 1 second, while HDPE crystallization begins only after 3.4 seconds as solvent evaporation nears completion.
knowledge_points.evidence: Crystallization of P3HT sets in within less than a second... Only when most of the solvent was evaporated did HDPE start to crystallize (t = 3.4 s).

knowledge_points.content: Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectroscopy (ToF-SIMS) of 1:1 DPP-TT-T:HDPE blends indicates a partial vertical phase separation where the semiconductor is enriched at both the gate dielectric interface and the top air interface.
knowledge_points.evidence: We find that the film is enriched with the semiconductor both at the bottom interface with the SiO2/OTS dielectric and at the top interface with air. Critically, a strong signal related to sulphur (S) is also found throughout the entire film.

knowledge_points.content: The threshold voltage shift (ΔVth) in DPP-TT-T transistors under a constant bias stress of -20 V is reduced from ~9 V in neat films to 2.5 V in 1:1 HDPE blends after 10,000 seconds.
knowledge_points.evidence: a threshold voltage shift of 2.5 V is recorded after 3 hours for 1 : 1 DPP-TT-T : HDPE blends. In strong contrast, neat devices exhibit a shift of close to 9 V at identical conditions/time periods.

knowledge_points.content: HDPE acts as a moisture barrier in N2200 blends, preventing the rapid degradation of electron mobility in air; neat N2200 mobility drops from 0.5 to 0.03 cm²/V·s over 8 hours, whereas 1:1 blends maintain significant performance.
knowledge_points.evidence: The electron mobility also starts to considerably decrease after 60 minutes... leading to a reduction of mobility to a value of only 0.03 cm2 V−1 s−1 in 8 hours. In stark contrast, devices fabricated with 1 : 1 N2200 : HDPE blends show a rather remarkable stability.

knowledge_points.content: The hydrophobic nature of HDPE, characterized by a low water permeability (PH2O) of 1.2–2.5 cm³·mm·10⁸/cm²·s·cmHg, protects the semiconductor/dielectric interface from water-induced redox reactions that cause charge trapping.
knowledge_points.evidence: We attribute this behaviour to the highly hydrophobic nature of HDPE, leading to a low permeation of water molecules... PH2O = 1.2–2.5 cm3 mm 108/cm2 s cmHg.

knowledge_points.content: Adding high-molecular-weight HDPE to N2200 during wire-bar coating enhances molecular orientation, increasing the dichroic ratio from 1.2 (neat) to 1.7 (blend) and improving charge-transport anisotropy.
knowledge_points.evidence: addition of the high-molecular weight HDPE assists to achieve molecular orientation during wire-bar coating. This is in agreement with the fact that we observe an increased optical dichroic ratio (DR) for blends of 1.7... while neat N2200 displays a DR = 1.2.
